name: Shortwave
summary: A radio button group drawn as the stations on an old tuning dial, with a gliding needle and a magic eye
about: A walnut tabletop radio whose five stations are a real radio group printed on the glass dial. Picking one turns the knob and glides the red needle along the scale until it wobbles to a stop, with static crackling in the speaker cloth and the green magic eye opening wide between stations. Once it locks on, the eye closes to a bright fan, the amber display names the station and the cloth glows to the beat with notes floating out.
how: Click a station on the dial, or Tab into the group and use the arrow keys to move between stations.
Use Fine tune (or drag the knob left and right) to search by hand and hear the static in between.
Watch the magic eye close as the signal gets stronger.
Press Power to switch the radio off, and again to warm the valves back up.
